sales_john: Quick intake — AcmePay (fintech) asking for Dedicated capacity sizing. They expect ~200 rps sustained for chat generation with p95 < 300ms, and ability to burst to 1000 rps for ~2 minutes during peak batch jobs. Model: gpt-neox-20b (8-bit), avg prompt ~60 tokens, avg completion ~120 tokens. They want a ballpark quote + recommended autoscale/burst policy. Any immediate red flags?
priya: thx John. couple quick clarifiers: 1) is 200 rps steady across 24h or peak window? 2) do they need session stickiness (KV cache per session)? 3) acceptable fallback to a quantized smaller variant during extreme overloads?
sales_john: mostly peak-window during business hours (08:00-20:00) with baseline traffic ~200 rps for ~6 hours. yes to session stickiness for user-level context (we'd keep KV cache pinned per user). they want minimal quality loss for fallback.
tim: rough back-of-envelope calc: 200 rps * (60+120)=36k tokens/sec sustained. burst 1000 rps => ~180k tokens/sec for 2 mins. GPU throughput for gpt-neox-20b 8-bit varies but assume ~6-8k tokens/sec per A100-80GB with optimizations. so baseline ~= 5 GPUs (36k/7k ≈5.1) but need headroom + autoscale => recommend baseline 6-8 GPUs. burst capacity ~24-30 GPUs to hit 180k tokens/s. this is a ballpark.
sophie: runtime notes: with KV caching pinned per user we can save ~30% tokens/sec for mid-conv requests but initial turn still costs full. autoscale policy suggestion: baseline pool 8 GPUs, scale up by +4 GPUs every 30s if queue > threshold, ramp cap 28 GPUs. keep a warm hot-pool of 4 gpus for sub-second startup to handle short bursts. for 2-min sustained bursts we should fully scale; also enable model-variant fallback to gpt-neox-6B-4bit for non-critical requests (configurable).
tim: add a sizing snippet for docs: ```
# sizing sketch
baseline_rps = 200
avg_tokens = 180
tokens_per_sec = baseline_rps * avg_tokens  # 36_000
gpu_tok_ps = 7000
baseline_gpus = ceil(tokens_per_sec / gpu_tok_ps)  # ~6
burst_rps = 1000
burst_tokens = burst_rps * avg_tokens  # 180_000
burst_gpus = ceil(burst_tokens / gpu_tok_ps)  # ~26
```
devon: can we get a quick price delta estimate for customer? they asked for monthly committed pricing vs on-demand burst. also what's lead time to reserve 26 gpus in Dedicated?
priya: on pricing — product needs a formal proposal but ballpark: committed baseline (8 gpus) + burst credits for on-demand will be cheaper than fully committing 28. ops: what lead time?@tim
tim: lead time depends on inventory and region; conservatively 2-4 weeks to provision Dedicated pool at that scale, faster if we reuse existing capacity in same cluster. billing: we can do commit for baseline + pay-as-you-burst for the extra, or tiered overage.
priya: action items: 1) devon — capture customer's hour-by-hour traffic profile and SLA (attach to thread). 2) tim + sophie — finalize a 1-page sizing + autoscale playbook with cost/lead-time ranges. 3) product — decide fallback model policy and rollout criteria. i'll add to backlog under "dedicated-capacity-intake" and tag for Q2-commit review.
capacity-bot: FYI — sizing playbook template: https://internal.redwood/sizing-playbook (use section "burst_patterns" and "warm_pool_recs"). :white_check_mark:
sales_john: got it. i'll upload the traffic CSV and the customer's acceptance criteria by EOD. thanks all :pray:
